quote: Any fool can write code that a computer can understand. Good programmers write code that humans can understand.
intro.p1: I'm a software engineer and economist with a multidisciplinary mindset and more than a decade of experience across engineering, finance and risk analytics. My background spans computer science, quantitative development, and financial modeling, supported by a BSc in Computer Science Engineering and an MBA with a focus on finance.
intro.p2: Over the years, I've worked in full-stack development, quantitative roles, and actuarial modeling, gaining hands-on exposure to enterprise software solutions in various fields. I've spent the majority of my career in multinational, English-speaking environments, where I've become known for being adaptable, curious, and quick to learn. I enjoy working in agile teams, value clean engineering practices like TDD, and naturally gravitate toward roles that sit at the intersection of technology and business.
intro.p3: I see myself as a generalist who learns fast, connects dots across domains, and understands customer needs just as well as the technical challenges behind them.
intro.p4: Outside of work, I'm usually exploring something new - especially astronomy, space research, photography. I also like to watch Formula 1 together with my fiancée and our cat.

aegon.modelDev.desc: We established a dedicated Model Development team after identifying a clear need for structured, high-quality model-building support across the company. I contributed to recruiting new model developers, shaping the foundations of our development workflow, and setting up the technical infrastructure for the team. This included version control, project-management tooling, CI/CD pipelines, branch-protection rules, and the integration of AI-assisted coding tools. Our team develops actuarial and financial models for various business units, supporting their modeling needs and decision-making processes with robust, well-governed solutions. I also presented at internal company conferences to help model owners and validation teams understand the benefits of disciplined model-development practices and stronger model governance.
aegon.validator.desc: I worked as a First Line Model Validator, performing non-independent validation of actuarial models to help model owners and developers prepare for the formal 2nd Line (Risk) validation. My responsibilities included understanding model methodology and implementation, identifying gaps in documentation or conceptual design, ensuring compliance and fitness for purpose, and supporting model owners in addressing issues before the independent review. I also contributed to establishing or gathering evidence for baseline testing and helped strengthen model governance and readiness across the validation cycle.
ms.quantDev2.desc: After transitioning to a full-time role, I continued supporting the global Fixed Income trading desks with automated reporting and reconciliation tasks, while taking on additional responsibilities. I occasionally contributed to people-management and recruitment activities within the team, supporting interviews and onboarding. My work remained focused on ensuring data quality, maintaining the reporting infrastructure, and collaborating closely with traders and strats to address time-sensitive issues in a fast-paced environment.
ms.quantDev1.desc: I supported bond traders and desk strats at Morgan Stanley by delivering automated reports that informed daily trading and risk-management decisions. I worked on the development and operation of a reporting platform that generated and distributed data to trading desks in New York, London, and Tokyo. During this period, I gained hands-on experience with Python and q/KDB, and deepened my understanding of economics, trading workflows, and market data. Beyond reporting, I also participated in reconciliation processes, helping identify and resolve discrepancies when different data sources showed conflicting information about the same trading activity.
avon.devOps.desc: After my development role at Avon, I moved into the DevOps team supporting the My Avon Store e-commerce platform. I worked on the operational side of the system, including 3rd-line technical support for issues that required code-level investigation, hotfixes, or changes beyond the scope of 1st and 2nd line support. I also participated in the 24/7 on-call rotation, handled production incident analysis, and contributed to scheduled releases of new platform versions. This role gave me hands-on experience with troubleshooting, patching, and maintaining a large-scale, customer-facing system in production.
avon.fullStack.desc: I was part of the My Avon Store development team, contributing to Avon's global e-commerce platform using technologies such as .NET C#, Node.js, MS SQL, MongoDB and Angular. As a member of the Market Expansion Team, my primary responsibility was to help introduce the platform to new countries, which included implementing region-specific features and integrations. This gave me the opportunity to work on payment provider integrations and other localization-focused development tasks that supported Avon's international rollout strategy.
abesse.fullStack.desc: I worked on the development and operation of custom enterprise software for clients across several industries. The delivery approach varied by project — from traditional waterfall to agile — giving me broad exposure to different methodologies. Early on, I contributed to an internal process-management tool for a domestic pharmaceutical company, and later focused on optimizing and extending the project-management system of an international energy provider. Throughout this period, I was part of a DevOps team, which allowed me to gain hands-on experience not only in development but also in operational and support responsibilities.
ht.fullStack.desc: I contributed to the development of a customer relationship management (CRM) platform, working in a Scrum/Agile environment and taking part in several greenfield projects. My work spanned multiple industries and included building project- and time-management tools for a U.S. public utilities company, as well as developing a digital reporting solution for the OBDK to support mandatory monthly and annual data submissions from healthcare institutions. I also created a mobile application for the HyperTeam CRM ecosystem, which gave me hands-on experience with the Xamarin platform.
